_about: Deliberately small starter vocabulary for how an organization works. Use this when no other ontology fits. A FIRST DRAFT to edit.
_summary: How an organization works: units, roles, processes, policies, systems and measures.
name: Operations Knowledge Base

Unit.definition: An organizational unit: a division, a department, a team.

Role.definition: A defined function someone performs. Attach work to a role, not a person.

Process.definition: A repeatable way of getting something done, made of steps.

Step.definition: One action within a process, with an owner and an input and output.

Policy.definition: A rule that constrains how work is done, internal or imposed.

System.definition: A tool or application the work runs on.

Measure.definition: Something the organization tracks to know whether the work is working.

Decision.definition: A choice made, with its reason and date. Superseded by a later one, never overwritten.

Document.definition: A source document in the corpus.

part_of.definition: A containment relationship: a unit within a unit, a step within a process.

performs.definition: The role that carries out a step.

belongs_to.definition: The unit a role sits in.

uses.definition: A system the work depends on.

supersedes.definition: This replaced that. Use with the temporal fields, never by overwriting.
